Mohican

This Mohican reading route begins with history written and revised by the Stockbridge-Munsee community and a Tribe-curated exhibition in its eastern homelands. The sources connect repeated movement with continuing cultural and political life. Keep the broader historical name, the present Stockbridge-Munsee government and other peoples with similar names distinct.

Mission House property, Stockbridge — context for Mohican Miles
Daderot, Mission House, Stockbridge, Massachusetts,21 August 2017; Wikimedia Commons; CC0 1.0.

Source & image record ↗ · CC0 1.0 — photographer’s explicit dedication

The property is context for the specifically documented Tribe-curated Mohican Miles exhibit in the eastern homelands, not a Mohican-built dwelling or the exhibit interior. Commons file-specific own-work identification, creator, date and explicit CC0 dedication inspected; downloaded 5472x3648 original and full frame visually inspected. The Trustees’ past-exhibition account establishes that the Stockbridge-Munsee Tribe curated Mohican Miles from its archives in the separate Carriage House behind the Mission House. This 2017 photograph gives property/institution context before that 2021-2022 exhibit. It is not an image of the exhibition, a Tribal dwelling, the Wisconsin reservation or an endorsement of the missionary history. The separate exhibition space is not claimed to be the main house shown. No crop or pixel editing made here. Complete available 5472×3648 source frame proportionally resized to 1800×1200 and JPEG recompressed; no pixel crop or retouching. Original source copy retained privately. Mohican histories connect the Hudson Valley with continuing communities, including the Stockbridge-Munsee Community in Wisconsin.

03

Following a community-authored history

Dorothy Davids’s brief history, revised by the Stockbridge-Munsee Historical Committee in 2017, follows movement from eastern homelands to Wisconsin and the rebuilding of community institutions. The selected pages describe Munsee relatives joining the community and the development of the Stockbridge-Munsee name. This is a community historical account with a stated revision history; it is not a complete genealogy or a substitute for the original records it discusses.

Read the sources [4] Stockbridge-Munsee Community / Historical Committee

04

A return through public interpretation

The Trustees’ account of the 2021–2022 Mohican Miles exhibition describes Tribal curation using the Arvid E. Miller Memorial Library Museum’s archives. The exhibition occupied the separate Carriage House behind the Mission House in Stockbridge, Massachusetts. This offers an example of the community shaping public history in its homelands. The dated exhibition notice does not establish current opening, access to every object or a later agreement’s implementation.

Read the sources [5] The Trustees of Reservations, exhibition host

Community-authored historical bookletStockbridge-Munsee Community / Historical CommitteeSource 4

A Brief History of the Mohican Nation: The Stockbridge-Munsee Band — selected pages ↗

Publication: 2017

Dorothy Davids’s community history, revised by the Historical Committee in 2017, connects repeated moves with the formation and rebuilding of the Stockbridge-Munsee community in Wisconsin.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Physical PDF pages 2-3,7 and 10 visually read, including title/acknowledgments and printed pages 4 and 7. The historical migration and rebuilding passages were compared with selectable text because the multi-column extraction interleaves columns. Other pages, maps, bibliography works, original treaty texts and present acreage/population were not reviewed or adopted. The booklet’s mistaken 1832 date for the Indian Removal Act is not repeated.

Review recorded: October 27, 2026

https://mohican-nsn.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/2017breif-history-1.pdf

Exhibition host’s collaboration accountThe Trustees of Reservations, exhibition hostSource 5

Mohican Miles — past exhibition ↗

Publication: 2021-2022

The host describes a Tribe-curated exhibition drawn from the Library/Museum’s archives at the Mission House property in Massachusetts. It supplies a concrete link between the Wisconsin community and public history in its homelands.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Full past-exhibition body read, including 2021-2022 dates, Tribal curation, the separate Carriage House behind the Mission House and the described agreement. Current opening, extension or future access were not established. Exhibition objects, their rights and repatriation records were not inspected.

Review recorded: October 27, 2026
